newsitem.title: USA: Jury says ABC, producer must pay $10 million for libel.
newsitem.headline: Jury says ABC, producer must pay $10 million for libel.

text.p: A jury on Wednesday awarded damages of $10 million to a bank executive who claimed he was libelled by ABC News in a television broadcast about real estate investments.
The jury deliberated for four days before returning the judgment in favour of BankAtlantic chairman Alan Levan and the company, Levan's attorney, Alan Fein, said.
The panel ruled that ABC, a subsidiary of Walt Disney Co., and its producer William Willson owed Levan $8.75 million and BankAtlantic $1.25 million.
"I think justice was done today," Fein said. "The jury saw a wrong and tried to right it."
ABC responded with a short statement saying it was disappointed with the jury award and planned to appeal.

Levan sued Capital Cities/ABC News in U.S. District Court over a programme segment called "Too Good to be True," aired on the network's 20/20 in November 1991. The story focused on a controversial swap of real estate partnerships for bonds at BankAtlantic Financial Corp.

BankAtlantic Financial Corp acquired partnership interests in exchange for company bonds in the late 1980s and early 1990s. BankAtlantic Financial sold much of the underlying property using some of the proceeds to help strengthen BankAtlantic.
Levan had sought $20 million, alleging that the ABC programme ruined his reputation by mischaracterizing the deals, ensuring he would never again be able to deal in real estate limited partnerships.

U.S. District Judge C. Clyde Atkins ruled earlier in the trial, which lasted about six weeks, that Levan could not seek punitive damages against ABC News because there was no evidence ABC had displayed ill will against Levan.
Fein said he would likely contest that ruling in the future.
